description_full: Garmin Ltd. designs, develops, manufactures, markets, and distributes a diverse range of GPS-enabled products and navigation, communications, sensor-based, and information products and services worldwide. It offers running; cycling products; smartwatch devices; scales and monitors; and sports timing and performance analysis; Garmin Connect and Garmin Connect Mobile, which are web and mobile platforms where users can track and analyze their fitness, activities and workouts, and wellness data; and Connect IQ, which enables third parties to create applications that run on Garmin devices. It also provides adventure watches; outdoor handhelds and satellite communicators; golf devices; consumer automotive; dog devices; InReach and Garmin Response; and dive devices. In addition, it designs, manufactures, and markets various aircraft avionics solutions, including integrated flight decks, electronic flight displays and instrumentation, navigation and communication products, automatic flight control systems and safety-enhancing technologies, audio control systems, engine indication systems, traffic awareness and avoidance solutions, ADS-B and transponders, weather information and avoidance solutions, datalink and connectivity solutions, and portable GPS navigators and wearables, as well as service products to the aviation market. Further, it offers chartplotters and multi-function displays, cartography, fishfinders, sonar, autopilot systems, radars, compliant instrument displays and sensors, VHF communication radios, handhelds and wearable devices, sailing, audio, digital switching, trolling motors, and lighting; and domain controllers and infotainment units, as well as software, map database, camera, wearable, and automotive solutions. The company sells its products through independent retailers, dealers, distributors, installation and repair shops, OEM, and online webshop. Garmin Ltd. was founded in 1989 and is based in Schaffhausen, Switzerland.
ceo_bio: Mr. Clifton  Albert Pemble | President, CEO & Director | Compensation: $1.4M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 23K people. Revenue per employee of $315K ranks in the below the sector median among Technology peers, improving at 6%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $59K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $7K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 5× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (8/10).
financial_summary: Garmin Ltd. is a large-cap technology business with a $55.0B market cap on $7.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 10% cost of capital — a 16-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 57% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.4B in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.98× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 15% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sector_headwinds.text: Price sits 43% above estimated fair value — no margin of safety left, and the cushion against estimate error has been bid away (confirmed by 2 other valuation measures)
Insiders are net sellers (100% sell ratio, net $5.0M) — the people closest to the business are reducing their personal stake
Technology sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 7% over 3 months
Elevated sector volatility (35% annualized) adds uncertainty
Late-cycle dynamics increase the probability of a slowdown
Antitrust and platform-regulation risk — the larger the network effect, the larger the regulatory target on its back, and a single consent decree can reset the moat.
AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sector_tailwinds: Reinvestment rate supports 13% organic growth capacity — capital is compounding inside the business
Operating margins 19% above sector median — the quantitative trace of pricing power
Altman Z comfortably in the safe zone — a fortress balance sheet on this measure
Founder-led — owner alignment that often matters more than any incentive plan
22 consecutive years of dividend payments — an operating record that makes the dividend claim credible
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment

sect: Its 26% operating margin runs 19pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.11x).
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-3.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 39% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 9% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 0.97, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $215.3M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 38% in the 2020 crash, 40% in the 2022 bear market and 83% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $199 (margin of safety -43%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 29%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $130 to $314 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: EV/EBITDA 22.0 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 40.4 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 61% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.5% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $299 on average, 5% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 26% clears the cost of capital of 9.6% by 16pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.23).
It runs a 57% gross margin and converts 19% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.2x equity multiplier).
It spends 15.5% of revenue on R&D and 2.3% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.7B (4% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 18.9, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 237 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 14.2% over 3 years, 11.6% over 5 years and 9.9% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 53% of profits supports about 13.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.5% a year over five years.
Capex runs 1.8x depreciation (3.7% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 28, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 14.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 58%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (13 sales, net $5.0M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.2% (1.5% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 22 consecutive years, raising it 8.1% a year over the last five.
people: With about 23,000 employees, each generates about $315K of revenue, 0.8x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 5.8% a year.
That works out to $59K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.4M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).

profile.head: Watch: priced 43% above its $199 fair value, but that value is low-confidence and the price is inside its $130–$314 range.
